skill.name: jira-workflow
skill.description: Orchestrate Jira workflows end to end with story proposals, approvals, issue creation, comments, and workflow transitions.
skill.summary: Manage Jira stories, approvals, comments, and workflow transitions from an AI coding workflow.

security_audit.summary: Most external command and certificate findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, and Jira issue key properties. Confirmed risks are authenticated Jira API calls and Jira credential handling through environment variables. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege token scopes, keep tokens in user-controlled environment variables, and never log or paste tokens.
Require explicit confirmation before creating issues, adding comments, or changing workflow status.
Validate the base URL against the expected Atlassian domain before sending the Basic Authorization header.
Include audited helper scripts in the package or remove script execution instructions from the documentation.

content.user_title: Manage Jira Workflows with Approval Gates
content.value_statement: Jira updates often drift from development work and require manual follow-up. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code propose stories, request approval, create issues, and sync workflow status.
actual_capabilities: Builds SAFe-style Jira story proposals with acceptance criteria and definition of done.
Prompts for user approval before creating Jira issues.
Shows Jira REST API calls for creating issues, subtasks, comments, and transitions.
Guides transition lookup for team-managed Jira workflow states.
Connects TodoWrite task progress with Jira issue status updates.
Documents required Jira environment variables, rate limits, and error handling.
limitations: Requires user-provided Jira Cloud credentials and project configuration.
Examples assume Jira REST API v3 and a team-managed project workflow.
Workflow transitions must be queried because each Jira project can differ.
Only SKILL.md was present in the scanned package; referenced script files were not included.

use_cases.title: Prepare approved Jira stories
use_cases.description: Turn feature requests into structured Jira story proposals before creating issues.

use_cases.title: Keep development status current
use_cases.description: Move Jira issues through Progressing and Done as coding work starts and finishes.

use_cases.title: Coordinate sprint execution
use_cases.description: Create subtasks, add implementation notes, and maintain workflow status during sprint work.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Jira story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jira story proposal for this feature. Include persona, goal, benefit, acceptance criteria, complexity, and subtasks. Ask for approval before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Create an approved issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved story details to create a Jira issue in my configured project. Link it to this epic if applicable, then report the new issue key.

prompt_templates.title: Sync work progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Start work on this Jira issue, update my task list, and add a concise progress comment. Query available transitions before changing Jira status.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a workflow cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full Jira workflow for this approved task. Create the issue, transition it when work starts, add implementation notes, and complete it after verification.

output_examples.input: Create a Jira story for password reset emails.
output_examples.output: A structured story proposal with user story text, acceptance criteria, subtasks, complexity, and an approval question before Jira creation.
A transition check, a Progressing status update when available, and a short confirmation with the issue key.

output_examples.input: Finish SCRUM-57 and record what changed.
output_examples.output: An implementation comment summary, a Done transition after verification, and a synced task status update.

best_practices: Confirm each Jira create, comment, and transition action before executing it.
Use a least-privilege Jira API token for the target project only.
Query available transitions before changing status in any Jira project.
anti_patterns: Do not create Jira issues from vague requests without user approval.
Do not assume workflow state names match across Jira projects.
Do not paste Jira API tokens into prompts, comments, or issue descriptions.

faq.question: Does this skill create Jira issues automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to ask for approval before creating Jira issues.

faq.question: Which Jira projects does it support?
faq.answer: It is written for Jira Cloud REST API v3 and team-managed workflows, with notes for classic epic links.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: It expects Jira email, API token, base URL, project key, and optional board ID environment variables.

faq.question: Can it transition Jira issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It queries available transitions, then posts the matching transition when one exists.

faq.question: Can it add implementation notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides examples for adding comments with files, commits, and completion notes.

faq.question: Are executable helper scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package only contains SKILL.md, although the text references scripts.
